input_quantity: MGMT promoter methylation beta -> r0 = 0.75 * (1 - beta)
input_source: MGMT beta panel: 140 patient(s) over 2 probe(s) [cg12434587, cg12981137], 292 record(s); calls at cutoff 0.358: methylated=37, unmethylated=103

arms.verdict: mtd/pfs_days: the input accounts for 10.7% of the total variance (sigma^2_between 107.708 vs sigma^2_within 895.214; F=1.24 on 139/140 df)
mtd/final_burden: the input accounts for 24.6% of the total variance (sigma^2_between 43069.1 vs sigma^2_within 132321; F=1.65 on 139/140 df)
steering/pfs_days: every donor and seed returned the same value, so there is no spread to attribute

steering/final_burden: the input effect is NOT resolvable above the model's own noise (MSB 1.80096 < MSW 6.99101, sigma^2_between = -2.59503 <= 0) -- the estimator's sign is the verdict, and it is not clipped

cannot_show: that this is a Bayesian credible interval: a credible interval is a posterior quantile, a posterior needs a likelihood, and this repository holds ZERO engine-output/patient-outcome pairs to build one from. The interval here is the empirical spread of a measured input propagated through the engine, with coverage over (donor, seed) jointly

that MGMT beta is the only uncertainty in the prediction: it is the one input this repository can measure per donor, and the engine's rate constants remain declared assumptions, so the input channel measured here is a lower bound on the true input uncertainty
that a band from donor tumours bounds the error for a NEW patient: the one-beta-per-case contract is a cohort distribution applied to a case
that the mapping beta -> r0 is right: it is a declared convention anchored on the calibrated default, and a different anchor moves every number in the band without any code changing
that the trial design is fixed: the switching arm saturates at the horizon, so its PFS readout has no spread to decompose and the conclusion drawn from it is about THIS design, not the policy family
